title: CPUNET nrfx_ipc.c duplicate-singleton adoption (P4 iteration 28, batch 3)

singleton_state.shipped_address_proof: R_ARM_ABS32 relocations into .bss.m_cb of the stock .text.nrfx_ipc_init / .text.nrfx_ipc_config_load sections resolved against the shipped image words.
singleton_state.our_link_stock_address: 0x21009178 (local 'b' symbol -- a linker PROVIDE cannot name it, so displacement of the owning unit is the only route)
singleton_state.reconstruction_pin: g_sdc_radio_context_area (a mis-name; the object is nrfx's IPC control block)
singleton_state.hazard: The stock nrfx_ipc.c is UNCONDITIONALLY linked in this build (nrfx_ipc_init / nrfx_ipc_config_load / nrfx_ipc_receive_event_enable / _disable / _irq_handler are all present), and it initialises ITS m_cb while the two reconstructions read the private relocation block.

unit_completeness.extent_proof: The five located sections tile the 408-byte run EXACTLY (76+120+56+56+100 = 408) with no gap, and the next byte 0x01034f24 is nrfx_timer.c's timer_configure.  The unit is stock and UNMODIFIED.
unit_completeness.reconstructed_subset: Only 0x01034d8c and 0x01034dd8 were ever reconstructed; 0x01034e50 / 0x01034e88 / 0x01034ec0 have no reconstruction in the corpus at all.

measured_liveness: MEASURED on /private/tmp/g1-i28b-net: FUN_01030bac (the recovered mbox_nrf_init, itself byte-identical to stock mbox_nrfx_ipc.c) has no referrer, so --gc-sections had ALREADY dropped both reconstructions from the ELF.  This displacement therefore closes the hazard permanently but is expected to leave the image unchanged; that expectation is checked, not assumed (see the report's build ledger).
